scope: Local normalized Snappy Parquet on the shared development host. Retained application disk cache; empty process caches at each restart. OS caches not purged, artifact GC disabled for isolated probes, readiness warming enabled. No cloud spend or provider qualification. No filesystem interposition or sampling during these measurements.
metrics_note: Health metrics refresh every five seconds; before/after samples are process snapshots, not instantaneous cache readiness. The after sample waits six seconds outside measured request latency. Initialization and provider traffic can include concurrent background warming. Hydration overlaps other aggregate phases.

probe_contract.first_search: database, five hits, score descending, projected HN metadata and body highlights, issued immediately after /tables responds.
probe_contract.cursor: AI, 128 hits per page, ten continuations and 1,408 unique hits. Resume the final continuation as the first query after process restart.
probe_contract.verification: First-search IDs/scores match the previously retained immutable reference. Cursor resumes preserve IDs, scores, projected source fields and highlights exactly; pagination repeats no IDs.

Hydration overlaps other phases; do not add it to them. Outside-lake time includes native/composed execution and transport; overlapping lake leaves can make it negative.

limitations: These samples are not a controlled before/after comparison and do not prove the historical 4.4-second ready-cache stall has been fixed.
The grouped stored-highlight acquisition contract is independently validated by a fresh native-source fixture; these HN timings do not establish its isolated speedup.
Full archive, raw BigQuery physical encoding, real S3/GCS and Antfly Cloud qualification remain outstanding.
